title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Teens of Baku. Tip #1
body: Get into TEAS, Baku Oxford, Dunya, or the international school, and immediately learn to read the drop-off line. If a black Gelandewagen pulls up and nobody gets out of the driver's seat, that's a driver, you're getting warmer. If they mention "our bag," "the place in Shahdag," or "we're at Sea Breeze all summer," warmer still. If they're doing IB or A Levels instead of preparing for the buraxilis imtahani, they're not staying in this country and everyone at that table already knows it. Never skip the group project as you might hear, "I'll just tell our driver to print it." Find the one whose tutor comes to the house instead of going to Hedef like a normal person, that's the tell, that's the whole tell. Then ask where they live. If they answer with only a building name, "Port Baku," "Crescent," "Badamdar," no street, no district, you're extremely warm. And if they switch to Russian with their mother on the phone without thinking about it once, congratulations, you have entered a different socioeconomic lobby.
caption:
Tip #1 of a series that is unfortunately extremely accurate 😭 Baku, you know exactly which drop-off line I mean.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Teens of Baku. Tip #2
body: Watch what happens in December. Everyone talks about the winter holidays, but listen to the specifics. "We're staying in Baku" is one lobby. "We're going to Shahdag for a few days" is a better lobby. "We're going to Shahdag and then Dubai and then my cousins in Istanbul" is the lobby you're aiming at. If they own ski equipment instead of renting it, you're getting warmer. If they're bored of Tufandag, warmer still. Ask what they did last summer, if the answer includes a summer programme at Oxford or Cambridge that was clearly more social than academic, you are very close. Never skip the trip the school organises abroad, that's the entire hierarchy in one bus. It's a sealed deal if they've been to more countries than they've been to districts of Baku, and they genuinely could not tell you how to get to Ahmadli.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 the December question tells you everything.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Teens of Baku. Tip #3
body: Learn the language switch, because in Baku it isn't a skill, it's an address. Azerbaijani with the driver. Russian with the family. English with the friends. All three in one conversation, none of it planned, that's the full set. If their grandmother speaks better Russian than Azerbaijani, that's not new money, that's Soviet-era Baku money, that's an apartment near Sahil with four-metre ceilings and a lift older than the country. If the family surname makes a waiter stand slightly straighter, you're getting warmer. Ask about the licence plate, or don't, just look at it, anyone can drive a Mercedes but not everyone has three of the same digit. It's a sealed deal if they have genuinely never held a Bakikart and could not tell you, under pressure, what a metro ride costs.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 the three-language switch is an address, not a skill.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Teens of Baku. Tip #4
body: Understand that you keep aiming at the loud lobby. The one in the Nike Tech tracksuit posting from the Badamdar villa is not the top of the pyramid, that's noise, that's money with a date of birth after 2010. The real one is quieter and slightly annoying about it. Plain clothes, no logos, no posts, a private account with forty followers who are all cousins. Went to Landau because the family cares about maths, not about being seen. Speaks three languages and apologises for their fourth. Will never mention money, will simply never once be inconvenienced by anything. If they don't understand why you're stressed about the fee, the deadline, the document, the appointment, congratulations, you have entered a different socioeconomic lobby. It's a sealed deal when you realise their family solves every problem with one phone call and they honestly think that's how phones work for everyone.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 you've been aiming at the loud one this whole time.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Teens of Baku. Tip #5
body: Wait for Grand Prix weekend, the city sorts itself automatically. If they complain that the road to their building is closed, you're warm, that means their building is on the track. If they say "we just watch from the balcony," you are very warm. If they have paddock passes and describe them as boring, you are home. Anyone can buy a grandstand ticket, only one kind of teenager is personally inconvenienced by Formula 1. It's a sealed deal if the family leaves the country that week because Baku becomes too crowded.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 F1 weekend is a class filter and everybody knows it.
